newsitem.title: USA: U.S. says Zaire is now high risk for business.
newsitem.headline: U.S. says Zaire is now high risk for business.

text.p: The U.S. State Department on Monday again urged businessmen and other private Americans to leave Zaire, where rebels are advancing on the capital Kinshasa.

"Our message is clear as a bell to the American private community. Get out of Zaire. Get out of Zaire before you find yourself in harm's way. They ought to listen to that message," department spokesman Nicholas Burns said.
Burns noted that there were missionaries in Zaire "who believe, obviously, that they are doing necessary work."
And there were "business people there who are chasing profits, chasing contracts, and obviously they and their companies have decided it's worth the risk," he added.
"We think it's a high risk, frankly," he said.
The United States earlier again reduced its official diplomatic presence in Kinshasa, from 37 to 25. Despite repeated appeals, Burns said that some 325 private Americans were still in the country.
He said one factor in U.S. decision-making was a flurry of rumours over the weekend that the Zairean goverenment was prepared to kill foreigners in order to draw in foreign intervention forces.
"Now we don't believe that rumour was true, but we have a responsibility to take it seriously, and so we have taken some very significant security precautions over the weekend," Burns said.
